university: The University of Texas at Dallas

documents.title: UTDSP5017 Generative AI Use in Academic Work
documents.summary: Policy delegating the permit, prohibit or partial decision to faculty. It requires syllabus and assignment communication, attribution when AI is permitted, and Code of Conduct enforcement for prohibited use.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no university-wide rule on AI use. It says 'Faculty have the discretion to permit, prohibit, or partially allow the use of generative AI', so the choice is left to each instructor, with permitted, partial and prohibited categories.

units.why: Defines the policy's purpose: 'a framework for the use of generative AI in academic work (including, but not limited to, coursework, independent research, dissertations, and theses)'. It sets scope and principles for the whole institution, so it is the framework type P56 and informs.
units.anchor: This policy provides a framework for the use of generative AI in academic work

units.why: Says 'Faculty have the freedom and responsibility to determine how generative AI can be used', so the decision is delegated to instructors (P04); it is addressed to instructors and made at course design.
units.anchor: Faculty have the freedom and responsibility to determine how generative AI can be used

units.why: Students 'are expected to uphold honesty, integrity, and service in all that they do, including when using generative AI'. It ties AI use to the existing Code of Conduct, so P77; P29 fits less because it is about owning submitted work.
units.anchor: students are expected to uphold honesty, integrity, and service in all that they do

units.why: States the aim of a learning environment that 'encourages ethical decision-making, academic and personal integrity, creativity, and innovation': a stated purpose for the framework, P56.
units.anchor: promote a learning environment that encourages ethical decision-making, academic and personal integrity, creativity, and innovation

units.why: 'Faculty have the discretion to permit, prohibit, or partially allow' hands the stance to each instructor, so P04. It also names three categories, which touches P05, but no tiers are defined here.
units.anchor: Faculty have the discretion to permit, prohibit, or partially allow the use of generative AI
units.fit_note: Also names three categories (permit, partial, prohibit), which touches P05.

units.why: 'Students should receive guidance from faculty members about the appropriate use of generative AI' sets an expectation that instructors communicate AI rules, P09 (P66 does not fit: no explaining of reasons).
units.anchor: Students should receive guidance from faculty members about the appropriate use of generative AI
units.fit_note: Framed as students receiving guidance, not specifically a syllabus statement.

units.why: 'Faculty must explain and communicate appropriate generative AI use to the student before academic work begins' is a mandatory timing rule for communicating expectations, P09.
units.anchor: Faculty must explain and communicate appropriate generative AI use to the student

units.why: 'the faculty member should provide usage details, including the citation style' tells instructors what to specify when they permit AI. P09 because it is about instructor communication; the citation element is noted.
units.anchor: the faculty member should provide usage details, including the citation style
units.fit_note: Also requires instructors to specify the citation style for AI use.

units.why: 'academic work produced by generative AI does not replace the student's understanding and interpretation of the course material' says AI must not replace the student's own thinking, P32.
units.anchor: does not replace the student’s understanding and interpretation of the course material

units.why: 'workforce-ready students may need generative AI skills and must learn appropriate workplace and academic uses' gives a career reason to learn AI use: P44.
units.anchor: workforce-ready students may need generative AI skills and must learn appropriate workplace and academic uses

units.why: Detailed statements 'should' appear 'in assignment descriptions and course syllabi' for permitted, partial and prohibited use: an instructor duty to put AI rules in the syllabus, P09.
units.anchor: faculty should include detailed statements in assignment descriptions and course syllabi

units.why: 'students are expected to use generative AI ethically and responsibly' is a general conduct expectation under permitted use with no specifics, so no type fits well; UNCOVERED rather than stretching P29.
units.anchor: students are expected to use generative AI ethically and responsibly
units.uncovered_note: When AI use is permitted, students must use it ethically and responsibly (a general conduct expectation without specifics).

units.why: 'Students should document and attribute the use of generative AI as appropriate to the academic style (APA, MLA, Chicago, etc.)' is a duty to disclose and cite AI use: P24.
units.anchor: Students should document and attribute the use of generative AI as appropriate

units.why: 'Students must follow written guidelines from faculty on citation styles' makes the instructor's citation guidance binding; disclosure rule P24.
units.anchor: Students must follow written guidelines from faculty on citation styles
units.fit_note: Emphasizes following the instructor's written citation guidelines.

units.why: 'Students must validate or verify the output from generative AI' is a verification duty: P31.
units.anchor: Students must validate or verify the output from generative AI

units.why: For partial use, 'students are expected to follow written guidelines provided by the faculty member' on what AI may do. It defines the partial category and binds students to the instructor's limits, so P05 (named category); P04 does not fit as well because the rule here is about following, not deciding.
units.anchor: students are expected to follow written guidelines provided by the faculty member
units.fit_note: Defines the 'partial use' category and binds students to the instructor's written limits.

units.why: Under partial use, 'Students should document and attribute the use of generative AI' repeats the disclosure duty for the partial category, so it is coded as its own unit: P24.
units.anchor: the use of generative AI as appropriate to the academic style (APA, MLA, Chicago, etc.).

units.why: 'Faculty should detail usage guidelines in assignment prompts' is an instructor duty to state AI rules per assignment: P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should detail usage guidelines in assignment prompts

units.why: 'When the faculty member prohibits use of specific generative AI tools, use is unauthorized and thus is a violation of UTDSP5003' classifies prohibited AI use as a conduct violation: P36.
units.anchor: use is unauthorized and thus is a violation of UTDSP5003

units.why: 'Students should present their work without the use of generative AI, including... ideating, outlining, writing, or studying, and creating text, tables, code' bans many uses when faculty prohibit. P19 is the nearest (no AI-produced work), but P01 is a default ban and this is conditional; the ban also reaches ideating and studying.
units.anchor: Students should present their work without the use of generative AI
units.fit_note: Under a prohibition it also bans ideating, outlining and studying with AI, beyond producing submitted work.

units.why: 'Given the integration of generative AI tools into commonly used tools, students should receive written guidance from faculty on which applications of generative AI are not permitted' covers embedded AI features: P07.
units.anchor: Given the integration of generative AI tools into commonly used tools
units.fit_note: Requires written instructor guidance about which embedded applications are not permitted.

units.why: 'Generative AI tools may not be used for any activity that would be considered illegal or fraudulent' is a general conduct ban: P74.
units.anchor: may not be used for any activity that would be considered illegal or fraudulent

units.why: AI may not be used in ways that violate 'state or federal law' or 'conflict with other UT Dallas or UT System policies': compliance with existing law and policy, P77, distinct from the fraud ban above.
units.anchor: conflicts with other UT Dallas or UT System policies

units.why: Everyone must 'adhere to university policies on Information Security and Acceptable Use and... FERPA when using generative AI': compliance with existing policy and law, P77 (P50 gives no data-handling specifics).
units.anchor: adhere to university policies on Information Security and Acceptable Use
units.fit_note: Names information security, acceptable use and FERPA as the policies to follow.

units.why: 'Any misuse of generative AI that results in academic dishonesty... will be subject to disciplinary action' treats misuse as misconduct handled by the Code of Conduct: P36.
units.anchor: will be subject to disciplinary action as outlined in the Student Code of Conduct
units.fit_note: Also covers misuse that endangers protected university or student data.

documents.unit: UT Dallas Office of Information Technology (Atlas knowledge base)
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI in Higher Education
documents.summary: IT explainer defining AI and Gen AI, listing pros and cons, giving best practices on data privacy and verification, and listing licensed tools and consultation channels.
documents.stance_why: The OIT article says the university 'advocates for its responsible use' and that 'Faculty and staff are encouraged to integrate these tools into teaching and research', while advising 'Do not use AI-generated solutions directly'. It is an advisory explainer, so the posture is permissive with conditions (verify, protect data).

units.why: Defines AI as 'computer systems and technologies designed to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence': a definition, P61.
units.anchor: computer systems and technologies designed to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence

units.why: Defines generative AI as 'a subset of AI technologies capable of creating new content': P61.
units.anchor: a subset of AI technologies capable of creating new content

units.why: 'AI-generated output should be reviewed critically and used responsibly' because 'AI does not possess human understanding, reasoning, or judgment': a verification duty, P31.
units.anchor: AI-generated output should be reviewed critically and used responsibly

units.why: The pros table lists 'Personalized Services - Tailors support to individual needs' as a benefit of AI in education, stated as a fact: P87.
units.anchor: Tailors support to individual needs

units.why: The cons table says 'Sensitive data may be exposed' as a privacy risk of AI. It is information, not a rule; P50 is the nearest type.
units.anchor: Sensitive data may be exposed
units.fit_note: Stated as a risk, not as a protective rule.

units.why: The cons table names 'May reflect training data biases' as a harm: P53.
units.anchor: May reflect training data biases

units.why: 'Cannot replace human decision-making' states a limit on AI. It is closest to P73 but only informational, so P73 with a fit note.
units.anchor: Cannot replace human decision-making
units.fit_note: Stated as a limitation of AI, not a rule that humans must decide.

units.why: 'The ease of generating content raises concerns about plagiarism and the authenticity of student work' gives an academic-integrity concern as rationale: P95.
units.anchor: raises concerns about plagiarism and the authenticity of student work

units.why: Notes Gen AI 'can inadvertently perpetuate biases present in their training data, leading to skewed or inaccurate outputs': P53.
units.anchor: Gen AI systems can inadvertently perpetuate biases present in their training data

units.why: 'not providing university, sensitive, research or personal data for training AI models' is a data-protection caution: P50.
units.anchor: not providing university, sensitive, research or personal data for training AI models

units.why: 'AI can streamline tasks such as grading, feedback, and course management' names a benefit for educators without conditions: P87, noting it touches faculty use.
units.anchor: AI can streamline tasks such as grading, feedback, and course management
units.fit_note: Names grading and feedback as efficiency gains for educators, without conditions.

units.why: 'OIT recommends reviewing prompt engineering methods using the CRISPE method' is advice on prompting: P93.
units.anchor: OIT recommends reviewing prompt engineering methods using the CRISPE method

units.why: 'Avoid entering university, personal, research, student, medical or sensitive information into public AI platforms unless confirmed they have a non-training agreement': data protection, P50.
units.anchor: Avoid entering university, personal, research, student, medical or sensitive information

units.why: 'Employ AI-generated content responsibly, ensuring academic integrity and transparency' is a general responsible-use direction; no specific type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Employ AI-generated content responsibly, ensuring academic integrity and transparency
units.uncovered_note: Use AI-generated content responsibly with academic integrity and transparency (a general best-practice statement).

units.why: 'Do not use AI-generated solutions directly' bars using AI output unmodified: P19.
units.anchor: Do not use AI-generated solutions directly

units.why: 'Always VERIFY the accuracy and relevance of AI-generated content before using it further' is a verification duty: P31.
units.anchor: the accuracy and relevance of AI-generated content before using it further

units.why: 'The guidelines are not formal or standard policy. They suggest best practices' states the advisory status of the ISO AI guidelines, a governance statement: P56.
units.anchor: The guidelines are not formal or standard policy
units.fit_note: States that the ISO AI guidelines are advisory best practice, not formal policy.

units.why: 'The University recognizes the transformative potential of AI and advocates for its responsible use' is an institution-level position, P56.
units.anchor: The University recognizes the transformative potential of AI and advocates for its responsible use

units.why: 'The Office of Information Technology (OIT) enables AI tools that meet security and privacy standards' states that OIT vets tools before enabling them: P65.
units.anchor: enables AI tools that meet security and privacy standards

units.why: 'Faculty and staff are encouraged to integrate these tools into teaching and research' encourages instructor AI use: P59.
units.anchor: Faculty and staff are encouraged to integrate these tools into teaching and research

units.why: Lists the tools the university offers, 'Microsoft Copilot', 'CometAI', 'Grammarly', 'Adobe Firefly', for students, faculty and staff: P92 (institution-wide provided tools).
units.anchor: These tools include enterprise solutions such as

units.why: 'Consult OIT: For personalized guidance on selecting and utilizing AI tools' is a consultation service open to users. P63 is faculty-only, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: For personalized guidance on selecting and utilizing AI tools and Models effectively
units.uncovered_note: OIT offers consultation on selecting and using AI tools.

units.why: 'Report AI/Gen AI Issue: To report any issues related to AI/Gen AI tools across campus to OIT' gives a reporting channel: P71.
units.anchor: To report any issues related to AI/Gen AI tools across campus to OIT

units.why: The policy summary 'Aligns AI use with the Student Code of Conduct and university policies' states the purpose of UTDSP5017: P77.
units.anchor: Aligns AI use with the Student Code of Conduct and university policies

units.why: 'By thoughtfully embracing Gen AI, UT Dallas aims to create an innovative and ethically responsible educational environment' is an institution-level orientation, P56.
units.anchor: UT Dallas aims to create an innovative and ethically responsible educational environment

notes: Course layer deferred in collect file; no school or computing policy found.
